class.craftsman.RUS: from a family of town artisans
class.landowner.RUS: from a family of service gentry
class.landowner.family.RUS: into a family of the service gentry
prof.monk.desc: The monastery: prayer, obedience, fasting. Worldly life is behind you, but the brotherhood will not let you starve.
prof.monk.desc.RUS: Vows in a monastery: prayer, obedience, copying books and labour on the monastery's land.
prof.icon_painter.desc: Boards, gesso, egg paints and a fast before the work. A good master is called even to the prince's cathedral.
prof.bortnik.desc: You climb pines to wild bee nests in hollowed trunks. Honey and wax sell well, but it is a long way down.
prof.fur_trapper.desc: In winter you go deep into the forest for sable, marten and squirrel. Furs are the great wealth of Rus, but the forest forgives no mistakes.
prof.bell_caster.desc: Copper, tin, a clay mould in a pit. Few men can cast a bell that rings true.
prof.druzhinnik.desc: You serve in the retinue of a prince or boyar: horse, mail, campaigns, a share of the spoils and a place at the prince's table.
prof.strelets.desc: A matchlock, a poleaxe and a red kaftan. You live in the musketeers' quarter, trade in your spare time and march out when the decree comes.
prof.farmer.desc.RUS: A light plough, a horse, rye and oats. You sow burnt clearings and old fields, and frost and rain decide the harvest.
prof.laborer.desc.RUS: You hire yourself to whoever has work: hauling timber, threshing, carrying sacks at the landing.
prof.artisan.desc.RUS: A smithy, a potter's wheel, a tannery or a cobbler's stall in the town quarter. Orders, apprentices and a crowded market.
prof.weaver.desc.RUS: Flax and wool: spinning through long evenings, weaving linen and cloth on the loom.
prof.midwife.desc.RUS: You deliver babies in the bathhouse and know herbs, charms and prayers, and which helps when.
prof.merchant.desc.RUS: Furs, wax, salt, cloth. The roads are long, with robbers and tolls at every portage.
prof.sailor.desc.RUS: You row boats along rivers and lakes and drag them overland at the portages. The pay is fair, but the rivers take their share.
prof.soldier.desc.RUS: When the prince calls up the levy, you take an axe, a spear and a shield and march.
prof.scribe.desc.RUS: You write charters, deeds of sale and books on parchment, and quick notes on birch bark. Few can write, and they are respected.
prof.physician.desc.RUS: Herbs, bloodletting, setting bones. Learned doctors are almost unknown; healers like you take their place.
prof.priest.desc.RUS: You serve a parish church: baptisms, weddings, funerals. You live off your parish and your own garden.
prof.priest.desc.slavic_pagan: You know the will of the old gods, divine, heal and lead offerings at the sanctuary.
prof.landholder.desc.RUS: Your own hereditary estate or a service holding: villages, peasants, dues and endless lawsuits with neighbours.
prof.magistrate.desc.RUS: You govern a town or district in the prince's name: courts, tribute and "feeding" off the locals.
prof.magistrate.desc.novgorod: The veche chose you as posadnik: you govern the city alongside the prince and the archbishop. Great honour, but the veche can also cast you down.
prof.matron.desc.RUS: The keys to the storerooms and cellars, the servants, the needlework, the winter stores: all of it is yours to run.
prof.household_slave.desc.RUS: You serve in the master's house: kitchen, stables, errands.
prof.field_slave.desc.RUS: An unfree labourer on a boyar's fields: you plough land not your own and live on what you are given.
prof.officer.desc.RUS: You lead a hundred men into battle and answer for each of them to the commander.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.RUS: Your own workshop in the town quarter, journeymen and customers among the boyars.
prof.shipowner.desc.RUS: Your own boats and hired boatmen; your goods travel the rivers from the Volga to the Baltic.
prof.official.desc.RUS: You run the household and courts on behalf of a prince or boyar. You have power, not love.
prof.official.desc.moscow: You serve in a government office: charters, decrees, seals. A clerk knows more about affairs of state than many a boyar.
prof.overseer.desc.RUS: A kholop trusted by the master with the keys, the stores and the other servants.
cause.rus_frost: froze to death on the road
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.RUS: Cabbage soup, porridge, rye bread, turnips and kvass
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.RUS: Fish, honey, game, berries and pies. Good for your health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.RUS: Feasts for the whole district: mead, roast swans, gusli players. Expensive
lifestyle.food.meager.desc.RUS: Goosefoot in the bread, thin soup. Your health suffers
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.RUS: Riding after game, wall-against-wall brawls on the ice. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.exercise.walks.desc.RUS: On foot to market, to Mass, to gather mushrooms. Free and healthy
lifestyle.medicine.home.desc.RUS: Herbs, the bathhouse and old women's advice
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.RUS: Prayer services, holy water, the relics of saints
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.slavic_pa: Charms, amulets, offerings to the old gods
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.RUS: A healer, or at court a foreign doctor. Expensive, but fewer die
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.RUS: Wash inside the stove or in the river
lifestyle.baths.sometimes.desc.RUS: Your own or a neighbour's smoke bathhouse once a week
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.RUS: Public bathhouses in town: steam, birch whisks, gossip, news. Must live in a town
focus.learn.desc.RUS: The sexton teaches letters: az, buki, vedi, then the Psalter. The family has to pay
focus.study.desc.RUS: Books, learned monks, the Psalter and chronicles. Costs money
focus.health.desc.RUS: The bathhouse, herbs, sleep and good food
focus.rest.desc.RUS: Feasts with friends, evening gatherings, swings at Maslenitsa
focus.religion.desc.slavic_pagan: Offerings, amulets, the feasts of Kupala and Kolyada
ev.festival.text.RUS: Maslenitsa! Pancakes, sledding down ice hills, wall-against-wall fist fights and a straw effigy of winter burned on a bonfire.
ev.festival.text.slavic_pagan: Kupala night: bonfires on the riverbank, wreaths floating on the water, leaping over flames and searching for the fern flower.
ev.a_eclipse.text.RUS: In broad daylight the sun went dark, as if someone had covered it with a hand. Dogs howled, women wailed about the end of the world, and then the light came back and everyone pretended they had not been frightened at all.
ev.a_stolen_tunic.text.RUS: While you were steaming in the bathhouse, someone took your best shirt from the changing room. You had to run home through the snow in somebody else's torn coat, wishing the thief everything you could think of.
ev.a_good_harvest.text.2.RUS: A generous year: the rye stands like a wall, sheaves are drying in the barn, and the flails beat on the threshing floor until dark. The cottage smells of fresh bread.
ev.t_honorary_decree.text.RUS: People remember that hungry year. The elders came to bow before you with bread and salt, the church holds a prayer service for you, and at feasts you are seated in the place of honour. People already speak of you the way the old songs speak of the righteous.
